reviewed_candidate.licensing_note: Licensing is plugin-specific; reviewed manifests include both MIT and proprietary entries.

external_effects: plugins can authenticate to third-party SaaS and developer platforms
connector-backed plugins can read and write remote application state
communication plugins can compose or send messages and email
developer plugins can create, edit, deploy, publish or administer code and infrastructure
finance and commerce plugins can interact with consequential account and transaction workflows
local skills and scripts can write project files and execute tool-specific commands
plugin creator tooling can create plugin directories, manifests, optional scripts, MCP definitions and marketplace entries
marketplace entries can point at external repositories outside the OpenAI repository

reviewed_subcapabilities.rationale: The marketplace mixes local OpenAI-curated bundles with external repository sources and multiple authentication policies; repository curation is not sufficient for blanket runtime admission.
Numerous plugins bind to remote MCP endpoints with authenticated access to SaaS or developer accounts and may expose write-capable tools.
Several plugins launch local Node or script-backed MCP servers and may access credentials, files, networks or generated artifacts.
The GitHub plugin is explicitly interactive/write capable and supports PR, issue, CI and publishing workflows.
Email, chat, calendar, drive and productivity plugins can access personal or organizational data and perform remote writes.
Developer-platform bundles include deployment, infrastructure, observability, security and source-control workflows whose authority must remain task-scoped.
Finance, investing, payments and commerce surfaces require independent domain and authority controls rather than marketplace-wide trust.
First-party provenance does not remove execution risk; reviewed OpenAI plugins can create API keys, write repositories, run local MCP services or instrument applications.
The creator skill writes plugin trees and marketplace metadata and can add MCP, hooks and scripts, so it requires explicit file-scope authority.
Marketplace entries that install from external repositories require their own provenance and capability audits; OpenAI marketplace inclusion does not substitute for upstream review.

narrower_admission_candidates.condition: Consider manifest/schema documentation as read-only reference material without installing plugins, executing scripts or connecting MCP servers.
Consider scaffolding only within an explicitly authorized workspace path, with marketplace mutation, hooks, scripts and MCP creation separately gated.
Audit only plugins needed for a concrete workflow, binding each decision to its exact manifest, skills, MCP endpoints, authentication and write surfaces.

rationale: The repository is a large curated marketplace rather than one uniform capability. It contains hundreds of skills, dozens of MCP/plugin manifests, hundreds of scripts, authenticated write-capable integrations and external repository sources. Blanket plugin-level admission would violate minimum-authority and provenance boundaries; individual narrow capabilities should be reviewed only when needed.
